summary: Gambit (@bolt-foundry/gambit, v1.0.0-rc.2) is a Deno-based agent harness whose CLI entrypoint is src/cli.ts (wrapped by bin/gambit as `deno run -A src/cli.ts`). It executes "decks" (Markdown/TS agent definitions) with `gambit run <deck> --message <text>`, looping model calls and tool calls until the assistant replies without tools. Model access goes through provider modules under src/providers: OpenRouter and Ollama use the OpenAI SDK's Responses API (`/v1/responses`, unusable with the proxy), Codex/Claude Code spawn external CLIs, and the Google provider uses the OpenAI SDK's chat.completions against GOOGLE_BASE_URL. The overlay therefore routes `google/<model>` through GOOGLE_BASE_URL=$PROXY_URL/v1 (OpenAI chat-completions API with tools), installs Deno 2.9.7 self-contained under /opt/harness, pre-caches the module graph offline, and adds a small coding-agent deck (/opt/harness/decks/coding_agent.deck.md) whose actions (run_shell, write_file, replace_in_file) operate in the task cwd; Gambit's built-in read_file/list_dir/grep_files/apply_patch/exec tools are also exposed. The run prints the final assistant text and writes a JSONL trace of every model/tool call to /out/gambit-trace.jsonl.
notes:
Verified locally with Docker (arm64): built on debian:bookworm-slim and on buildpack-deps:jammy; check_command passes offline (--network none) in both; a full run against a scripted mock proxy made 6 POSTs to /v1/chat/completions (model sent as "gemini-2.5-pro", tools array included), executed run_shell/write_file/replace_in_file plus the built-in read_file, created and edited a file in the mounted cwd, wrote /out/gambit-trace.jsonl (38 events), printed the final reply and exited 0. The repo working tree stayed clean.

Key choices and caveats:
- Provider routing: Gambit's OpenRouter and Ollama providers only call client.responses.create (POST /v1/responses), which the proxy does not serve; the Codex/Claude Code providers shell out to external CLIs. The Google provider (src/providers/google.ts) uses the OpenAI SDK chat.completions with tools and optional streaming, so the model name must carry the google/ prefix (router strips it before sending). GAMBIT_MODEL is consumed by the run_command via --model-force (which overrides the deck's modelParams); the harness itself has no model env var. Do not set OPENROUTER_API_KEY.
- The deck under /opt/harness/decks is an addition, not a modification: Gambit needs a deck to run, and the bundled "gambit bot" deck is TUI-only and restricted to GAMBIT_BOT_ROOT. Its action decks import gambit-core by relative path because the restricted inspect worker only allow-lists locally reachable imports (bare import-map specifiers failed with a read-permission error).
- Built-in tools (read_file, list_dir, grep_files, apply_patch, exec) are auto-exposed with -A but resolve relative paths against the deck directory and exec has a 30s cap and no shell, hence the custom actions and the prompt instruction to pass absolute paths to built-ins. The run_command injects the absolute cwd into the first user message.
- The launcher passes --unstable-worker-options (required by the default worker sandbox; the repo's CI parity script enables the same unstable flag) and --cached-only/--frozen against a copy of deno.lock so nothing is fetched or rewritten at run time. /etc/profile.d/harness.sh restores PATH under `bash -lc`, but the commands use absolute paths anyway.
- --message is JSON.parse'd when it is valid JSON; the "Repository working directory: ..." prefix guarantees it is treated as plain text. --state is not used because it requires a pre-existing workspace.sqlite. Streaming (--stream) is intentionally off: the streaming path indexes chunk.choices[0] and would break on usage-only chunks.
- Dockerfile uses RUN heredocs (BuildKit, Docker 23+ default). Deno version pinned to 2.9.7 (latest at time of writing); the deno.lock format v5 needs Deno >= 2.2.
- Guardrails: maxPasses 400 model turns, no wall-clock timeout; run_shell defaults to a 600s per-command timeout.
